well: IODP Expedition 308 Sites U1319/U1320/U1322/U1324 - Ursa Basin and Brazos-Trinity Basin IV, continental slope, GULF OF MEXICO offshore Louisiana; 32 penetrometer deployments (DVTPP + T2P probes) including EIGHTEEN at Site U1324 spanning 50-608.2 mbsf - the measurements that make U1324 the catalogue's FIRST co-located measured temperature AND pressure site
operator_on_log: Flemings, Long et al. (Penn State / UT Austin) - Davis-Villinger Temperature-Pressure Probe (DVTPP) and the purpose-built Temperature/dual-Pressure (T2P) probe, deployed from JOIDES Resolution, IODP Expedition 308 (2005); T2P temperatures reached formation equilibrium (no extrapolation applied, per the table's own note)
source_database: IODP Proceedings vol. 308, data report 203, Table T2 (doi:10.2204/iodp.proc.308.203.2008) - the temperature companion to the catalogue's existing PANGAEA 725472 pore-pressure entry from the SAME expedition program; transcribed verbatim from the publisher's HTML table

fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the publisher's HTML table page - COMPLETE table (all 32 deployment rows, all 12 columns) in one fetch; transcribed verbatim including blank cells and the T2P dual-port 'a; b' paired cells
coverage: COMPLETE TABLE: 32 deployments across 7 holes at 4 sites - BOH 50-608.2 mbsf / 1105.7-1759.9 mbsl; hydrostatic pressure u_h, overburden sigma_v, decay times, three pore-pressure extrapolations, and equilibrium temperatures 5.66-16.09 degC (T_end) with T_1/t where extrapolated (DVTPP rows only)
curves: BOH [mbsf] 50-608.2 (depth index) + BOH [mbsl] (dual depth, per-hole water-depth identity)
u_end / u0-1/t / u0-1/sqrt(t) pore-pressure extrapolations [MPa] (T2P rows carry dual-port 'a; b' pairs verbatim)
T_end [degC] all 32 rows + T_1/t [degC] DVTPP rows only (T2P at equilibrium, no extrapolation - the table's own note)
source_anomaly_disclosure: Preserved verbatim with three disclosures: (1) T2P rows leave T_1/t BLANK by design (probe reaches equilibrium; the table's own note says no extrapolation was applied) - blanks are not missing data; (2) dual-port T2P pressure cells hold 'a; b' semicolon pairs verbatim - the reader maps them to NaN in numeric channels and NEVER splits or averages them (the verbatim cells stay in the file); (3) re-deriving the report's bilinear U1324 thermal gradient from T_end by simple least-squares gives 19.9 C/km above 360 mbsf and 17.0 below, vs the report's stated 18.6/16.7 - consistent in structure (bilinear, steeper above) but not numerically identical because the report's fit methodology (station selection, T_1/t usage) is its own; both are recorded, neither is repaired
purpose: FIFTY-FIRST catalogue entry, and the FIRST under the new co-location selection rule (strata-inference standing direction, 2026-08-28): not a new region or a new kind for its own sake but THE MISSING COLUMN for an existing site - the independent evaluation's score-changing criterion verbatim ('one new assembly with measured temperature AND pressure'). Eighteen U1324 stations at 50-608.2 mbsf overlap the existing PANGAEA 725472 measured pore pressures, so assemble_u1324 gains a measured temperature component (hole-filtered U1324B/C rows) and the engine bridge that REFUSED u1324 until this column existed now ACCEPTS it: the catalogue's third runnable well, and its first with BOTH coordinates of the engine's state measured in the formation itself
verified: 32 rows x 12 columns complete; per-hole water-depth identity (BOH mbsl - BOH mbsf constant within each of the 7 holes, U1324B = 1056.8 m EXACTLY matching the assembler's pre-existing water_depth_m constant); hydrostatic gradient u_h/mbsl = 10.042-10.049 kPa/m seawater on ALL 32 rows; sigma_v > u_h on all 32 rows; U1324 station count = 18 matching the report's own claim; bilinear gradient structure re-derived (steeper above 360 mbsf) with honest numeric disclosure; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical table
